narrative: The model estimated your probability of bad credit at 43.0%. Although that is below half, it was still above the bank’s approval cutoff for this application, so the loan was denied. The most influential factor was your savings position: having at least 1,000 DM in savings worked in your favor and pushed the decision toward good credit. It was the strongest feature in the assessment, and your savings level is stronger than that of most approved applicants, only a small share of whom have savings at that level. The second most important factor was the amount requested: 10,961 DM, far above the approved average of about 3,020 DM. This pushed substantially toward bad credit because a much larger loan increases repayment exposure. The third most important factor was your employment duration of four to seven years, which also worked in your favor and pushed toward good credit by reflecting stable employment. Even so, the large requested amount, together with other less influential aspects of your profile, outweighed the positive signals from savings and employment and placed you above the denial threshold. To improve a future application, consider requesting a smaller amount closer to the approved average, continuing to build savings, and maintaining stable employment. You could also ask the bank which specific affordability or policy cutoff applied and whether a lower loan amount would be considered.
